tools.name: request_human_review
tools.description: Use this when building or revising an eval set, LLM-as-judge prompt or rubric, and you need the user's own judgment on example outputs. Send the rubric and 1 to 50 cases (input, output, optional context, optional verdict and reason from your own judge). Returns a review link for the user, a review i

tools.name: get_human_judgments
tools.description: Read the user's pass / fixable / fail verdicts and reasons for a review created with request_human_review, without waiting. Returns progress, every verdict so far, the cases where the user disagreed with your judge, the agreement rate, and a next step. Treat the user's verdicts as ground truth for t

tools.name: wait_for_human_review
tools.description: Call right after showing the user the review link. Waits until the user has finished grading (or timeout_seconds passes, at most 240), then returns the same result as get_human_judgments. If it returns before the user is done, call it again or ask the user how it is going.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_human_review, get_human_judgments · Private data: request_human_review · Public sink: request_human_review · Destructive: request_human_review, get_human_judgments.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_human_review, get_human_judgments · Private data: request_human_review · Public sink: request_human_review · Destructive: request_human_review, get_human_judgments

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
